messages.subject: Re: Exposing dendrogram data to Javascript
parts:
Mike, did you install the repo as an R package? You shouldn't need to look at the files at all unless you want to modify them.

if (!require("devtools"))
  install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("d3-heatmap", "jcheng5")

In your ui.R and server.R, make sure to library(heatmap) [I should probably change the name] so heatmapOutput and renderHeatmap can be found.

You can also play with it without writing your own Shiny app by calling heatmap::showHeatmap(x) where x is a numeric matrix.

parts:
Gotcha.  I didn't know how to add additional parameters, each attempt just broke it, so instead I just changed the input to a list.  I just incorporated the existing color ranges functions from gplots.  For anyone who may be interested in changing the colors:

renderHeatmap <- function(expr, env = parent.frame(1), quoted = FALSE) {
  func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
 
  function() {
    data <- func()[[1]]
col=func()[[2]]
    matrix <- as.matrix(data)
   
    rng <- range(matrix)
   
    #   rowClust <- hclust(dist(matrix))
    #   matrix <- matrix[rowClust$order,]
    #   colClust <- hclust(dist(t(matrix)))
    #   matrix <- matrix[,colClust$order]
    tmp <- tempfile()
    png(tmp)
    hm <- heatmap(data, keep.dendro=TRUE)
    dev.off()
    unlink(tmp)
    rowClust <- as.hclust(hm$Rowv)
    colClust <- as.hclust(hm$Colv)
    matrix <- matrix[hm$rowInd, hm$colInd]
   
    rowDend <- hclustToTree(rowClust)[[1]]
    colDend <- hclustToTree(colClust)[[1]]

   
    domain <- seq.int(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 100)
    require(gplots)
   
        if (length(col) == 1 && is.character(col)){
        colz <- get(col, mode = "function")
    colors <- colz(100)
    colors <- sub('FF$', '', colors)
}

    matrix <- list(data = as.numeric(t(matrix)),
                   dim = dim(matrix),
                   rows = row.names(matrix),
                   cols = names(matrix),
                   colors = colors,
                   domain = domain)
   
    return(list(rows = rowDend, cols = colDend, matrix = matrix))
  }
}

#' @export
showHeatmap <- function(mat) {
  shiny::runApp(
    list(
      ui = basicPage(
        heatmapOutput('heatmap')
      ),
      server = function(input, output) {
        output$heatmap <- renderHeatmap(
          mat
        )
      }
    )
  )
}

 renderHeatmap <- function(expr, env = parent.frame(1), quoted = FALSE) {
  func <- exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
 
  function() {
    data <- func()[[1]]
col=func()[[2]]
    matrix <- as.matrix(data)

        if (length(col) == 1 && is.character(col)){

in server.r:
library(heatmap)

renderHeatmap <- function(expr, env = parent.frame(1), quoted = FALSE) {
  func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
 
  function() {
    data <- func()[[1]]
col=func()[[2]]
    matrix <- as.matrix(data)
   
    rng <- range(matrix)
   
    #   rowClust <- hclust(dist(matrix))
    #   matrix <- matrix[rowClust$order,]
    #   colClust <- hclust(dist(t(matrix)))
    #   matrix <- matrix[,colClust$order]
    tmp <- tempfile()
    png(tmp)
    hm <- heatmap(data, keep.dendro=TRUE)
    dev.off()
    unlink(tmp)
    rowClust <- as.hclust(hm$Rowv)
    colClust <- as.hclust(hm$Colv)
    matrix <- matrix[hm$rowInd, hm$colInd]
   
    rowDend <- hclustToTree(rowClust)[[1]]
    colDend <- hclustToTree(colClust)[[1]]

   
    domain <- seq.int(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 100)
    require(gplots)
   
        if (length(col) == 1 && is.character(col)){
        colz <- get(col, mode = "function")
    colors <- colz(100)
    colors <- sub('FF$', '', colors)
}

    matrix <- list(data = as.numeric(t(matrix)),
                   dim = dim(matrix),
                   rows = row.names(matrix),
                   cols = names(matrix),
                   colors = colors,
                   domain = domain)
   
    return(list(rows = rowDend, cols = colDend, matrix = matrix))
  }
}

     if(is.null(input$dataset))
return()

browser() # it doesn't even reach the browser, despite the 'traditional' heatmap passing all of those ifs

tempdat=heatd$tempdat
colr=heatd$colr
mat=list(tempdat,colr)
